title: Session work through Cosmo and the move to baritone
summary: Cosmo Matassa called the core of Bartholomew's band for sessions; he switched to baritone alongside Lee Allen on tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Um... Let's see how it's low. So it's low. So it's low. So it's low. So it's low. So it's low. How did you see the recording sort of an industry here? Were you... When are you starting to do session work? I mean, outside of Dave? When are you starting to get the, you know, an independent call?

Well, that came through Cosmo. That came through Cosmo. After we had done the recordings with Dave Bartholomew, there were calls that would come in that for Cosmo to get some musicians together. And the recording, the studio band was the nucleus of the Dave Bartholomew band. Earl Palmer, Frank Fields, Ernest McElaine, and I had, they brought in Lee Allen from the Paul Gatons band to do it. And I was playing tenor, he was playing tenor, and somebody said, well, Ray, why don't you get a baritone? So I did.
Was... Did you... Why the switch to baritone? Why was the...

Because I think that Lee Allen was a... more of a funky saxophone player, what he called for. I was more into bebop, even though I played tenor and baritone on a lot of rhythm and blues and rock and roll. You know, I played on all of them. But I thought he was better.
Yeah, I always wanted to ask you, did you acquiesce to Lee? Because I... To me, I always thought you were just as good, but you were always playing Barry.
